question: On 24 November 2023 the German Bundesrat gave its assent to the Future Financing Act (FFA), which the German Bundestag had adopted only a few days earlier (on 17 November 2023). It has yet to be signed into law by the Federal President. As a result of an amendment, the FFA now also provides for a cooling-off period.

At EU level, it was decided not to introduce a cooling-off period as such, with consumers being expressly given a three-day period for reflection only where a loan is subject to the taking out of payment protection insurance (‘tying practices’).

Accordingly, the provisions of the amended Consumer Credit Directive adopted by the EU are in clear contradiction to the cooling-off period provision inserted into the FFA as a result of an amendment. The EU Consumer Credit Directive came into force on 19 November 2023 and must be transposed into national law within 24 months.

That means that no legislative measures may be adopted that conflict with the directive and furthermore that national provisions diverging from it are expressly prohibited (Article 42 of the Consumer Credit Directive). 1.
Is the Commission aware of the inconsistency between the abovementioned FFA and the EU Consumer Credit Directive?
Does the Commission share the legal misgivings about the German FFA in relation to the Consumer Credit Directive adopted on 19 November 2023, and what does it intend to do about this?
answer: Directive (EU) 2023/2225 on credit agreements for consumers (1) entered into force in November 2023. It repeals Directive 2008/48/EC (2) with effect from 20 November 2026. The national transposition process of Directive (EU) 2023/2225 is ongoing. Member States shall adopt and publish by 20 November 2025 the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this directive.

They shall immediately communicate the text of those provisions to the Commission. The Commission will examine the correct and full transposition of the directive from all Member States, including Germany, following the transposition deadline and provided that Member States have officially communicated their specific national measures transposing the corresponding provisions of the directive.

Directive (EU) 2023/2225 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 October 2023 on credit agreements for consumers and repealing Directive 2008/48/EC, OJ L, 2023/2225, 30.10.2023. Directive 2008/48/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 April 2008 on credit agreements for consumers and repealing Council Directive 87/102/EEC, OJ L 133, 22.5.2008, p. 6666-92.
